name: Raḍī al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Ghafūr al-Lārī
summary: Jāmī's disciple in Herat, whose gloss on his teacher's commentary on al-Kāfiya, the Ḥāshiya of ʿAbd al-Ghafūr, was read with it in the madrasas of India and the Ottoman lands.
bio: ʿAbd al-Ghafūr came from Lār in southern Iran and became one of the closest disciples of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Jāmī in Herat, in the Naqshbandī path as in learning; he wrote a supplement to Jāmī's lives of the saints and a commentary on parts of his works.

His Ḥāshiya on Jāmī's al-Fawāʾid al-Ḍiyāʾiyya explains the commentary on al-Kāfiya where its reasoning is close; in the Dars-i Niẓāmī it was read with Sharḥ Jāmī, and the lithographs of India print it in the margin. He died in Herat in 912/1506.
